Walkthrough solver

Active techniques

These are the methods currently active in the solution walkthrough. Every logical move is checked against the displayed completed grid before it is shown.

Step 0

Snyder notation

Lists each currently legal digit in every empty cell as a pencil mark.

Logical placement

Naked Single

Places a digit when an empty cell has only one remaining candidate.

Set logic

House Single

Uses one of the eight specified nine-cell tuples, each of which contains all digits 1–9 exactly once, to place a digit that has only one remaining location in that tuple.

Intersection

Locked Candidates

When a digit in a complete region or set tuple is confined to its overlap with another unit, that digit is removed from the rest of the overlapping unit.

Candidate elimination

Naked Pair

When two cells in the same row, column, or Squishdoku region share exactly the same two candidates, those candidates are removed from the other cells in that unit.

Candidate elimination

Naked Triple

When three cells collectively contain exactly three candidates, those candidates are removed from the other cells in that unit.

Candidate elimination

Naked Quadruple

When four cells collectively contain exactly four candidates, those candidates are removed from the other cells in that unit.

Candidate elimination

Hidden Quadruple

When four digits are restricted to the same four cells in a unit, other candidates are removed from those cells.

Fallback

Brute Force

Used only when the active logical techniques cannot progress. It places a target-verified value and adds 10,000 to the difficulty rating.

Eliminated pencil marks are shown in red with a strike-through for one step. Original givens are black; solver-filled values are blue.
